broadcastIntroPolicy: Most existing songs already contain the broadcaster at the front. The final eight should add music and atmosphere, not duplicate announcer IDs. Only the closing piece may carry a signoff if needed.

tracks.title: Coffin Lid Rag
tracks.direction: 1930s spooky rag / hillbilly swing instrumental, upright feel, creaky room energy, no modern country production, no announcer needed.

tracks.title: Dead Air Interlude
tracks.direction: Short weak-signal instrumental, muffled old radio tone, sparse steel guitar and static, no big build, no announcer needed.

tracks.title: Roaster Rattle
tracks.direction: Mechanical coffee-roastery rhythm, old rockabilly / steel guitar, dark playful Halloween machinery, vintage not modern, no announcer needed.

tracks.title: Black Cat Boogie
tracks.direction: Fast playful 1940s/50s spooky rockabilly boogie, slap bass, hollow-body guitar, hand percussion, Halloween fun without modern country gloss.

tracks.title: Lanterns in the Fog
tracks.direction: Slow eerie vintage instrumental, distant steel guitar, brushed drums, low organ, foggy small-town night feeling, restrained and atmospheric.

tracks.title: Boiler Room Bones
tracks.direction: Clanking haunted-machine rhythm with bones/percussion illusion, old swing and hillbilly accents, playful PG-creepy energy, no crowd and no modern production.

tracks.title: Last Cup Before Dawn
tracks.direction: Lazy late-night vintage closer, warm tube-radio feel, restrained and sleepy, coffee-roastery imagery without sounding like a cafe; broadcaster only if naturally integrated.

tracks.title: The Town Goes Quiet
tracks.direction: Creatures, ghosts, goblins and beasts are moving away; town winds down after the night's escalation; relaxed end-of-show feeling. A normal announcer may sign off at the end only if the song needs the final show close.
